source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Routine magnesium is recommended for every polymorphic VT episode even when the QT is normal","B":"Magnesium replaces immediate unsynchronized shock when sustained polymorphic VT is unstable","C":"Magnesium may be considered to suppress recurrent torsades associated with long-QT polymorphic VT","D":"Magnesium is contraindicated in torsades because it predictably lengthens ventricular repolarization"}}
source_row.rationale: Current AHA adult advanced life support guidance recommends immediate unsynchronized shock for sustained polymorphic VT. Magnesium may be considered for recurrences of polymorphic VT associated with long QT (torsades), but routine magnesium is not recommended when the QT is normal.

source_row.stem: A client has recurrent torsades de pointes associated with a prolonged QT interval. Which statement about IV magnesium is accurate?
